requirements.requirement: Log every sudo command run on node1, with user and timestamp, to /var/log/sudo-commands.log
requirements.summary: A sudoers drop-in (/etc/sudoers.d/99-sudo-logfile) sets Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log", log_input, log_output, and was validated with visudo -cf. Test sudo commands produced entries in the dedicated log showing timestamp, invoking user (antrieb), effective USER=root, and the COMMAND run. This was demonstrated both pre- and post-reboot.

requirements.requirement: Keep sudo command log entries out of the general system log (/var/log/secure, /var/log/messages)
requirements.summary: The sudoers drop-in includes !syslog to suppress syslog-based command logging. Tail of /var/log/secure before and after the test sudo commands, and after reboot, showed only generic PAM session opened/closed lines with no COMMAND= text; an explicit grep for COMMAND= in secure log post-reboot returned no matches.

requirements.requirement: Configuration and logging behavior persists correctly across a node restart (provider-wide restart evidence protocol)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (95e2f83d...) and healthy config/log baseline were captured, systemctl reboot was acknowledged, the node was confirmed unreachable mid-restart, post-restart boot_id (414ae4e3...) differs confirming an actual reboot, and after recovery the sudoers drop-in was intact/valid, the log file persisted with prior entries plus a newly appended sudo command, and the secure log remained free of COMMAND= entries. This matches the fixed after-prepare/after-executor boot-identity cross-check (95e2f83d... -> 414ae4e3...).

overall_summary: The executor satisfied both material outcomes of the task: sudo commands on node1 are now logged with user, timestamp, and command to a dedicated /var/log/sudo-commands.log via a validated sudoers.d drop-in with !syslog, and verified command-level entries no longer appear in /var/log/secure or /var/log/messages. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was also executed well, with clear pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, an observed unreachable window, a changed boot_id proving an actual reboot, and full post-restart recovery of the sudoers config, persisted log data, correct routing, and a newly logged post-reboot command. Operational hygiene is high, with only a trivial leftover /tmp/reboot.log artifact from the reboot invocation.
limitations: Package-health checks were unavailable (timed out) in both before-prepare and after-executor snapshots, so native package-manager consistency could not be cross-checked.

The permission-denied failure on cmd-e381eb406af1454a's unqualified 'cat' of the sudoers file is a minor script defect that was immediately corrected in the following command; it does not indicate a functional gap but is noted for completeness.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor actions were tightly scoped to the task: creating the sudoers drop-in, setting file permissions, adding a companion logrotate policy for the new log (reasonable, low-risk best practice directly tied to managing the required log file), and running bounded test/verification commands. No unnecessary or unrelated mutations were found in the command trace. One minor residue: the reboot was launched via 'nohup sudo -n systemctl reboot >/tmp/reboot.log 2>&1 &', which left /tmp/reboot.log behind after the node came back up (visible in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot); this is a small, low-risk artifact tied directly to the mandated restart-evidence step and was not cleaned up. cmd-e381eb406af1454a's plain 'cat /etc/sudoers.d/99-sudo-logfile' failed with permission denied (file is 0440 root:root) and was immediately corrected in the next command using 'sudo -n cat', which succeeded — a self-corrected read-only slip, not a mutation or residue.
